record.context_brief: sampling sets for STFT phase retrieval
record.original_question: Fix a sufficiently regular window function for the short-time Fourier transform. Which spiral-like or more general sampling sets in the time-frequency plane are informative enough to determine a function, up to global phase, from sampled STFT magnitude measurements?

evidence.quote: Question 8.7. Fix any sufficiently “nice” window function w. Do uniqueness results hold for spiral-like sampling sets Ω ⊂ R2? More generally, what exactly determines when a given sampling set Ω is sufficiently informative to allow for recovery of f up to a global phase from |Vwf|2_Ω?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ be a fixed window function (assume sufficient regularity and decay, e.g., $w$ in the Schwartz class or in the Feichtinger algebra, with $w \neq 0$). For $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the short-time Fourier transform of $f$ with respect to $w$ by
$$ V_w f(x,\xi) \;=\; \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\,\overline{w(t-x)}\,e^{-2\pi i\,\xi t}\,dt, \qquad (x,\xi)\in\mathbb{R}^2. $$
Two functions $f,g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ are said to agree up to a global phase if there exists $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ with $g = e^{i\alpha} f$. Given a set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, we say $\Omega$ is a uniqueness set for phaseless STFT sampling with window $w$ if, for all $f,g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, the equality
$$ |V_w f(x,\xi)| \;=\; |V_w g(x,\xi)| \qquad \text{for all } (x,\xi)\in \Omega $$
forces $f$ and $g$ to agree up to a global phase.

(a) Determine whether spiral-like subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$ (for instance, sets of the form $\{(r(t)\cos\theta(t),\, r(t)\sin\theta(t)) : t \ge 0\}$ for suitable monotone $r$ and $\theta$) are uniqueness sets for phaseless STFT sampling.

(b) More generally, give a characterization of those sampling sets $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ that are uniqueness sets for phaseless STFT sampling with window $w$.
artifact.status_search_result: Sampled STFT phase retrieval is a very active topic. It is known that uniform lattices never give uniqueness for a single window (Grohs–Liehr non-uniqueness theory), while alternatives such as square-root lattices, multi-window setups, and pairs of parallel lines have been shown to yield uniqueness. However, no general characterization of uniqueness sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is known, and uniqueness for spiral-like sampling sets does not appear to be established in the literature found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Non-Uniqueness Theory in Sampled STFT Phase Retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: No window and no lattice yield unique recovery of every L^2 function from phaseless STFT samples.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice sampling cannot give a uniqueness set for single-window STFT phase retrieval.

status_evidence.title: Phaseless Sampling on Square-Root Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Square-root lattices enable unique recovery of any square-integrable function via phaseless STFT-sampling.
status_evidence.claim: Non-lattice sampling sets can serve as uniqueness sets, motivating the broader characterization question.

status_evidence.title: Multi-window STFT phase retrieval: lattice uniqueness
status_evidence.snippet: Multi-window approach bypasses discretization barriers and yields lattice uniqueness.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses but does not fully resolve the general question of which sampling sets are informative enough.
